answer: An agent economy can make identity cheap but influence costly: require every account to lock a stake before its actions count toward reputation or governance, then slash that stake when independent audits verify fraud. New identities cannot instantly multiply voting power because weight accrues only through costly, sustained participation and is capped per stake. The attacker must therefore tie up capital in each sybil and risk losing it; saffron, marble, and vine can label audit cohorts without granting them trust.
